column1: # Revetsec's expected outcomes for the Project Wycheproof signature and MAC vectors (plan M2-9), as the primitive
# runner com.revetsec.internal.crypto.WycheproofSignatureTests observes them. The vectors are C2SP/wycheproof's
# Reason codes are VerifyResult and KeyRejectedException.Kind names.
# Format (see WycheproofSignatureTests.Expectations): one line per exception, five TAB-separated fields:
#   file <TAB> tcId=<n> or rule:<name> <TAB> jdk <TAB> outcome <TAB> note
# jdk is all, <n>, <n>+ or <n>-<m> (Java feature releases, 17 and up); outcome is accept, reject:<code> or n/a.
# A vector with no line expects accept if upstream marks it valid, and any rejection if invalid; every acceptable
# vector needs a line. A #count line pins a file's outcome counts, reason by reason, on the releases it names; each
# file has exactly one for every release. A stale, duplicate or overlapping line, or a count that no longer holds,
# Outcome counts, measured on Corretto 17.0.20.1, 21, 25, 26 and 27 (21 and later agree).
# ECDSA (IEEE P1363): SunEC on JDK 17 rejects a valid signature whose x(R) is at least n, which needs a reduction
# mod n (plan section 9.6); JDK 21 and later accept it. An honest signature hits this with probability below 2^-129.
